Bank Manager Refuses to Provide Details About a Cyber Crime-Related Hold or Freeze? Know What You Can Do
Your bank account may be restricted due to a cybercrime complaint processed through NCRP-CFCFRMS. But the bigger problem is often finding out why the restriction was imposed and what you need to do next.
You may be told, “Raise a request on the GRM Portal.” In such a situation, don't rely only on verbal communication.
Here’s what you should do:
Submit a written application to the bank asking for the available details of the restriction, disputed transaction, reference number, and concerned LEA/IO.
Submit your explanation and supporting documents showing the genuineness of the transaction.
Ask the bank to process your grievance through the prescribed GRM/CFCFRMS mechanism. Under the SOP, the bank is expected to submit the grievance within 7 calendar days.
Take an acknowledgement and keep copies of all documents, correspondence and reference numbers.
If the matter remains unresolved, use the prescribed review and appeal mechanism. The SOP provides for review by the District Grievance Officer, appeal to the State Grievance Officer, and ultimately an approach to the jurisdictional Court.

Most importantly, keep everything in writing. A proper documentary trail can make your grievance much easier to pursue.

comment: A key practical challenge is the gap between account restrictions and timely information flow. Banks and LEAs need stronger coordination so genuine customers aren't left navigating multiple channels without clarity.
